oneOf.description:
The agent is being paused on its machine (`cntrl pause`): who paused it
and why. The gateway answers `paused`; the agent then hangs up and stays
away until someone resumes it there.
The gateway has recorded a pause.
The alert rules this device decides itself (D43), the whole set.

sid.description: Session ID, also covered by the signature.

Challenge.description: The gateway's first frame. The agent signs `nonce` in its [`Hello`].

target.description:
Rust target triple of the build, such as `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`. It
picks the release artifact for an update.

machine_id_hash.description: SHA-256 of the machine ID, never the raw ID.

AgentInfo.description: The agent build and the machine it runs on.

gen.description: Key generation counter. A mismatch locks the device (close 4403).

sig.description:
Signature over the challenge's sid and nonce, the gateway host, the IDs
and `gen`, base64url without padding.

HelloAuth.description: Proof of possession of the device key.

oneOf.description: ECDSA with P-256 and SHA-256.

SigAlg.description: Signature algorithm of the device key.

Caps.description:
What the device's policy lets Console call: operation and topic names with
the version of each, plus optional protocol features.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the normalized policy; empty when no valid policy is in force.

error.description: Why no valid policy is in force. The agent then denies everything.

PolicySummary.description: The device policy in force, by hash.

Hello.description:
The agent's first frame: who it is, proof of its device key, and what its
policy lets Console call.

HeartbeatConfig.description: How often the agent pings, and how long it waits for a pong.

Limits.description: Limits the gateway enforces on this session.

acked_upto.description: Highest outbox `seq` Console already has; the agent resends the rest.

subs.description: Subscriptions to restore after a reconnect.

credential.description: A renewed connection credential; the agent keeps it for its next connect.

Welcome.description: The gateway's answer to a valid [`Hello`].

via.description: What carried the request, such as the dashboard or a named API token.

id.description: ULID, also the audit ID on both sides.

actor.description: Who asked, recorded for audit and never used for authorization.

idem.description: Retries of non-idempotent operations reuse this key, so they act once.

retry.description: Whether retrying the same request may succeed.

ErrorCode.description:
Why an operation failed. Stable within a protocol major version; a code from
a newer revision decodes as `Unknown`.

Progress.description: Progress on a running request, before its [`Response`].

Cancel.description:
Asks to stop a running request. It is still answered by a [`Response`], with
`cancelled` if it stopped in time.

oneOf.description: A rule the device decides fired or resolved (`records::AlertRecord`).

Records.description: Records from the agent's outbox, delivered at least once.

Ack.description: Confirms every record up to and including `upto`.

ReconnectWindow.description: A random delay between `min_ms` and `max_ms` spreads reconnects out.

GoAway.description:
Asks the agent to disconnect and come back within a window, for example
during a gateway deploy.

by.description: The account that paused it, as the machine names it.

Pause.description: Pausing the agent on its machine, as `cntrl pause` does.

Paused.description: The gateway's answer to `pause`, once it has recorded it.

rev.description:
When the rule last changed, in Unix milliseconds: a changed rule starts
over, resolving what it had firing.

minutes.description: How many minutes in a row the condition has to hold.

target.description:
What the reading is of: a mount point for a disk, a sensor kind (`cpu`,
`gpu`, `disk`) for a temperature, a GPU's name; absent for any of them.
For a `service` rule, the service's name, as `service.restart` takes it.

threshold.description:
The line, in the metric's unit: percent for `cpu`, `memory`, `swap`,
`disk_used`, `gpu_busy` and `gpu_memory`; GiB for `disk_free`; the load
average itself for `load`; degrees Celsius for temperatures.

oneOf.description: A reading beyond a line.
A service that isn't running.
A kind from a newer hub; the agent skips the rule.
A reading from a newer hub; the agent skips the rule.

AlertMetric.description: A reading a rule watches, judged by each minute's average.

AlertRules.description: Every rule this device decides, replacing any before.

NoParams.description: Parameters of operations that take none: `{}` or an absent `data`.

arch.description: CPU architecture as Rust names it, such as `x86_64` or `aarch64`.

boot_time.description: When the machine booted, in Unix seconds.

machine.description:
The machine, such as `Mac mini (Mac16,10)`, `Dell Inc. OptiPlex 7090`
or `Raspberry Pi 4 Model B Rev 1.4`, where the OS says. From 0.1.4.

chassis.description:
The form factor, in systemd's words (machine-info(5)): `desktop`,
`laptop`, `convertible`, `server`, `tablet`, `handset`, `watch`,
`embedded`, `vm` or `container`, where the machine says. From 0.1.10.

version.description: `VERSION_ID`, such as `24.04`; absent on rolling releases.

name.description:
Such as `Apple M4` or `AMD Ryzen 7 5800X 8-Core Processor`; ARM boards
often don't say.

threads.description: Hardware threads, which the OS schedules as CPUs.

performance_cores.description: On CPUs with two kinds of core, such as Apple silicon, how many of each.

ServiceList.description:
`service.list`: the services the device's service manager knows: system-wide
(systemd's system units; launchd's system domain), then on macOS what runs
in each logged-in user's session.

unit.description:
The name `service.restart` takes: a unit such as `nginx.service`, or a
launchd label.

description.description:
What it is, when the service manager says: systemd's description.
launchd keeps none.

detail.description:
The service manager's own words for the state, such as systemd's
`active (exited)` or launchd's last exit status.

pid.description: The main process, while it runs and the service manager reports it.

protected.description: The device policy keeps service actions off it.

scope.description: Where it runs; system-wide when absent.

user.description: For `user` scope, whose session it runs in.

kind.description: What it is; a service when absent.

enabled.description:
Whether it starts at boot, where that can be changed: a systemd unit
file that's enabled or disabled, or a third-party LaunchDaemon on a Mac.
Absent for units that can't be enabled (systemd's `static` ones), for
Apple's own jobs, and from agents before 0.1.5.

ServiceStatus.description: One service and how it is.

oneOf.description: Its process is running.

It ran and finished cleanly, such as a oneshot unit or an on-demand job
between requests.
Loaded but not running, and not since it last stopped cleanly.
It stopped with an error.

ServiceState.description: A service's state across service managers.

oneOf.description: System-wide: systemd's system units, launchd's system domain.

A logged-in user's session: on macOS, their GUI domain, with their
LaunchAgents and the apps they have open.
A daemon, agent or unit that the service manager runs.

An app open in a user's session. Its `unit` is the app's bundle ID and
its `description` the app's name.

user.description: Whose session; the one user logged in when absent.

force.description:
Quit at once, as Force Quit does, losing unsaved work. Otherwise the app
is asked to quit the way the Dock asks, and may ask to save first.

AppQuit.description: `app.quit`: one app to quit, named by its bundle ID as `service.list` gives it.

oneOf.description: It closed.
Asked to quit, it's still open: it may be asking to save changes.
It wasn't open.

started.description:
Its start time from the process table, in Unix seconds. A process that
started at another time has taken the PID over, and is left alone.

force.description:
Kill it at once with SIGKILL, losing anything unsaved. Otherwise it gets
SIGTERM and a few seconds to exit.

ProcessSignal.description: `process.signal`: one process to stop, as the process table named it.

oneOf.description: It exited.
It's still running after the wait: it may be ignoring SIGTERM.
It had already exited, or its PID now names another process.

scope.description: Where the service runs; system-wide when absent.

user.description: For `user` scope, whose session; the user at the console when absent.

ServiceRef.description:
Names one service: a systemd unit such as `nginx.service`, or on macOS a
launchd job's label, such as `homebrew.mxcl.nginx`.

ServiceJob.description: The outcome of a service job.

JobResult.description:
A job result, as systemd reports it in `JobRemoved`. On macOS it is `done`
once launchd shows the job running again (or finished cleanly), `failed` if
it exited with an error, and `timeout` if launchd doesn't say in time.

actions.description:
The actions this machine can take. One can be held off by an inhibitor
and still be listed.

sessions.description: Who's signed in, at the machine or remotely.

inhibitors.description: Programs holding off a shutdown or sleep, through logind on Linux.

unlock_after_restart.description: What a restart waits for before the machine can reconnect.

restarts_after_power_loss.description:
Whether the machine starts by itself after a power cut, where the agent
can tell (macOS's `autorestart`).

wake_on_lan.description: The wired interface a magic packet would wake, where there is one.

PowerAction.description: A power action, by the name of its operation's second part.

place.description:
Where: a seat or terminal, such as `seat0` or `console`, or the address
a remote login came from.

what.description: What it holds off, such as `shutdown` and `sleep`.

mode.description: `block` holds the action off; `delay` only delays it a few seconds.

Inhibitor.description: A program holding off a shutdown or sleep.

oneOf.description: FileVault: the Mac waits at the unlock screen for a password.

Linux's root filesystem is encrypted, so the machine may wait for a
passphrase at boot, unless a TPM or network unlock is set up.

DiskUnlock.description: Why a restarted machine waits before it can reconnect.

mac.description: Where a magic packet goes, such as `d0:11:e5:73:0e:f0`.

enabled.description:
Whether it's set to wake the machine; absent where the agent can't
tell.

PowerStarted.description: What a power action returns: that it has started.

owners.description:
Whether the processes were found. Finding them takes root, so privd
does it; without privd the ports come alone.

address.description:
The address it's bound to: `0.0.0.0` or `::` for every address,
`127.0.0.1` or `::1` for this machine only, or one of the machine's.

service.description: The service it runs in: a systemd unit, or on a Mac a launchd job.

Listener.description:
A socket waiting for others: a TCP socket listening, or a UDP socket bound
and not connected.

note.description:
Why there's nothing to say, when there isn't: on Linux, that
smartmontools isn't installed.

disk.description: The disk's name, as `storage` gives it.

wear.description:
How much of an SSD's rated life is used, as a percentage; it can pass
100.

detail.description: What's wrong, in a few words, when something is.

DiskHealth.description: What one disk says of its health.

oneOf.description: The disk passes its own check.

It passes, but something is past a limit or was once: worn out, too
hot, errors logged, attributes that crossed their threshold.
It says it's failing.
It can't say, or wasn't asked, as a disk asleep isn't woken for this.

interval_ms.description: Sample interval; the agent raises anything below 1,000 ms to 1,000 ms.

swap.description: Absent when the machine has no swap.

disk_io.description:
Reads and writes across the machine's physical disks, over the sample
interval.

network.description:
Traffic across the machine's physical network interfaces, over the
sample interval. Tunnels and container networks aren't added, since
their traffic crosses a physical interface too.

filesystems.description:
The machine's filesystems, as of the last look; the agent looks every
10 s.

temperatures.description: Temperature sensors, as of the last look; the agent looks every 5 s.

gpus.description: GPUs, as of the last look; the agent looks every 2 s.

CpuStats.description: CPU use over the sample interval.

available.description: What the kernel estimates new work can use (`MemAvailable`).

DiskIo.description: Disk throughput, in bytes per second.

NetworkIo.description: Network throughput, in bytes per second.

mount.description: Where it's mounted, such as `/` or `/mnt/media`.

name.description: The volume's name where the OS gives one, such as `Macintosh HD`.

used.description:
In use. On a Mac it's the whole APFS container's use, since its volumes
share the space.

available.description:
What a user other than root can still write; on Linux the blocks kept
for root aren't in it, so used and available don't add up to the total.

label.description: The sensor's name for people, such as `CPU` or `nvme0`.

oneOf.description: The CPU, or the chip on Apple silicon.
Anything else, including kinds from newer agents.

name.description: Such as `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090` or `Apple M4`.

memory_used.description: Memory in use; on Apple silicon, what the GPU has of the shared memory.

GpuStats.description:
A GPU's readings. Each is absent where its driver doesn't give it: Apple
silicon shares the system's memory, so it has no total, and only some
drivers report temperature and power.

sort.description: Highest CPU first (the default), or highest memory.

limit.description: At most this many rows, 1 to 500; 50 when absent.

query.description:
Keeps the processes whose name, user or unit contains it, ignoring
case, or whose PID it is.

ts.description: When the table was read, in Unix milliseconds.

matched.description: Processes that matched the query, before the limit.

ProcessesSample.description:
One `processes` event: the top of the process table, as the subscription
asked for it.

cpu.description:
CPU since the previous reading, as a percentage of one core, so it can
pass 100 on a machine with several.

started.description:
When it started, in Unix seconds. With `pid`, it names the process to
`process.signal`.

unit.description: The systemd unit it runs in, on Linux.

kernel.description: A kernel thread, which can't be stopped.

protected.description:
The device won't stop it: it's part of the operating system, it's the
agent, or its unit is one the device policy protects.

ProcessInfo.description: One process, with its threads folded in.

unit.description:
One service's log, such as `nginx.service`; the whole system's when
absent.

user.description:
The user whose session runs `unit`, for a user's LaunchAgent on a Mac;
the system's service when absent.

priority.description:
The least important to show, as a syslog priority: 0 (emergency) to
7 (debug); everything when absent.

grep.description: Only lines whose message contains this, ignoring case.

lines.description: How many earlier lines come first: 0 to 1,000, and 100 when absent.

include_os.description:
Whether the whole system's log takes in the operating system's own
processes: on a Mac, Apple's processes and subsystems and the kernel,
which make nearly all of it. Everything comes when absent; Linux takes
everything either way.

only.description:
Only lines from these sources, named as entries name them; every
source when empty.

skipped.description:
Lines left out since the last batch because they came faster than the
agent sends them.

ended.description:
Why no more lines will come, such as the log reader stopping; absent
while the log is live.

one_in.description:
While new lines come faster than the agent sends them, it sends an
even sample of about one in this many; absent while it sends them all.

counts.description:
How many new lines each source logged since the last batch, sampled
or not: the busiest 20.

LogsBatch.description: Log lines, in the order they were logged.

ts.description:
When it was logged, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; 0 when
that isn't known, as for the earlier lines of a service's output file.

source.description: Who logged it: the service, the program's name, or the output file.

interval_ms.description: How often to send, in milliseconds: 2000 when absent, 1000 at least.

ts.description: When it was read, in Unix milliseconds.

routes.description:
Where traffic for elsewhere goes: one default route per address family
that has one.

dns.description: The name servers the machine asks, as its resolver names them.

name.description: As the OS names it, such as `eth0`, `enp3s0` or `en0`.

label.description: The port's name where the OS gives one, such as `Wi-Fi` on a Mac.

physical.description:
Hardware, not a bridge, tunnel or container link, whose traffic also
crosses a physical interface.

speed.description: The link's speed in megabits per second, where the OS knows it.

received.description: Bytes per second since the previous reading.

received_total.description: Bytes since the interface came up.

errors.description: Packets that failed, sending or receiving, since it came up.

oneOf.description: A VPN or tunnel: WireGuard, `tun`, `utun`, GRE and the like.
A container's or a virtual machine's link: `veth`, `docker0`, `virbr0`.

address.description: IPv4 or IPv6, without the prefix, such as `192.168.1.20`.

gateway.description: The next hop, such as `192.168.1.1`; absent for a point-to-point link.

interface.description: The interface the route leaves by.

interval_ms.description: How often to send, in milliseconds: 2000 when absent, 1000 at least.

ts.description: When it was read, in Unix milliseconds.

disks.description: The physical disks, not partitions, RAID or device-mapper devices.

name.description: As the OS names it, such as `sda`, `nvme0n1` or `disk0`.

external.description: Plugged in over USB or Thunderbolt, or removable media.

reads.description: Requests completed per second, where the OS counts them.

wait_ms.description:
How long a request took on average, queueing included, in
milliseconds; absent when none completed.

busy.description:
The share of the time it had requests in progress, 0 to 1. A disk
that serves requests in parallel, as an SSD does, can take more while
at 1 (iostat(1), %util).

Disk.description: A physical disk, with its traffic since the previous reading.

oneOf.description: A solid-state disk on SATA, SAS or USB.
A spinning disk.
A disk a hypervisor provides.

mount.description: Where it's mounted, such as `/` or `/mnt/media`.

name.description: The volume's name where the OS gives one, such as `Macintosh HD`.

source.description:
What's mounted: a device such as `/dev/nvme0n1p2`, or for a network
volume its server and share.

disk.description: The physical disk it's on, by name, when there's one.

used.description:
In use. On a Mac it's the whole APFS container's use, since its volumes
share the space.

available.description: What a user other than root can still write.

inodes.description: Files it can hold, where the filesystem has a fixed number.

network.description: Mounted from another machine: NFS, SMB and the like.

pop.description:
The device key's signature over [`signing_string`], base64url without
padding.

previous.description:
The device this machine is enrolled as now, if any, so the gateway can
retire it when the new one is created (D23).

replace.description:
Go ahead when `previous` is in another organization, or replace it in
the same one. Without it the gateway asks first: `confirm_move` or
`already_enrolled`, leaving the token unused.

key.description: The uncompressed P-256 point, base64url without padding.

machine_id_hash.description: SHA-256 of the machine ID, never the raw ID.

sig.description:
The previous device key's signature over [`replace_signing_string`],
base64url without padding.

PreviousDevice.description: The device a machine is enrolled as, proven with that device's key.

key_id.description: ID of the device key, carried in every hello.

credential.description:
The connection credential: a ticket the gateway checks before a
connection reaches its hub, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Opaque to the
agent; the gateway renews it in a `welcome`.

replaced.description: The device this enrollment replaced, now removed from its organization.

from.description: For `confirm_move`: the organization the machine is in now.

oneOf.description: The machine is already in the token's organization; nothing changed.

The machine is in another organization; enroll again with `replace`
to move it.

period_ms.description: How long the period was, in milliseconds.

StatsRecord.description:
`metrics`: host stats over about a minute. CPU is averaged from counter
deltas across the period, with its busiest sample beside it; load and memory
are the last values read.

busy.description: Busy time across all cores over the whole period.

busy_max.description: The busiest sample in the period.

seq.description: The sequence number of the last record it covers.

head.description: SHA-256 of that record's line, lowercase hex.

key_id.description: The audit key's ID, from enrollment.

sig.description: ES256 over [`checkpoint_signing_string`] with the audit key, base64url.

AuditCheckpoint.description:
`audit_checkpoint`: privd's signature over the head of the device's audit
log. Console keeps them, so the log can later be checked against them.

rev.description: The rule's `rev` the agent judged it by.

since.description: When the condition began, in Unix milliseconds.

at.description: When the agent decided, in Unix milliseconds.

value.description:
The minute's reading that decided it, in the rule's unit; absent for a
service.

peak.description: On resolving, the furthest past the line it went while firing.

AlertRecord.description:
An `alert` record: a rule this device decides fired or resolved (D43). The
outbox keeps it until the hub has it, so it survives a dropped link.
